doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Monk, Ellington and Archie Shepp in the 1970s
title: Meeting Duke Ellington at the recording studio
summary: At the Ellington sessions Ware plays along with Duke, and worries he cannot read the music.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Cat Anderson was in the band, and Julian Priestley and I went down just before we went to work, we went down to Masie Hall where they were getting it together, you know, Joe Benjamin. Duke Ellington's valet, a friend of mine, he said, "Man, I want you to meet Duke." I said, "Well, I met Duke before," which I had out in Chicago, back in the '60s. Paul and I were hanging out one night at E. Parker McDougall (PHONETIC) and Paul Gonzalves say, "Man, you probably bring

Wilbur down to the studio," -- we recording down there tomorrow -- he says, "I want Duke to hear him." (Unintelligible) John Lamb was playing bass with him and they were talking about trying to get me in the band. Well, I was crazy to (unintelligible) accept a gig because I had too much respect for Duke, you know, to get in the band and know he'd be writing music and all that and I couldn't read it. However, the cat was telling me, say, "Man, Duke don't write no music for basses, you know, unless he's got a special concert or something like that."

But anyway, I go, and he's sitting around and they were recording and Duke, in between while they was changing tapes, Duke's playing the piano, you know, and the rest of the cats are milling around and John Lamb was standing up there with his (unintelligible) bass -- Duke's playing something like the blues. I asked John, "Let me play along with Duke," and I did. I enjoyed that very much. Duke looked up from the piano, just kept playing, looked at me, and we had a good little rapport. I didn't have a chance to say nothing to him because we had to go right into the numbers. When I come out of the studio, we walked to the little rest area, Johnny approached me, John Hodges (unintelligible) looking kind of strange. He shook my hand, you know. I was really in awe of the guy. He was so great. Real giants, I had always looked up to that band and Carney, Cootie, everybody. It was just marvelous being in their presence.
